'''Ravindra Nath Sudan''' (also called Ravi Sudan; June 8, 1931 – January 22, 2009) was an Indian-American [[Electrical engineering|electrical engineer]] and [[physicist]] who specialized in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/theithacajournal/obituary.aspx?n=ravindra-nath-sudan&pid=123195620&fhid=7263|title=Ravindra Sudan Obituary|last=|first=|date=2009|website=Ithaca Journal|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11609044.html|title=Sudan, R. N.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref> He was known for independently discovering the whistler instability in 1963, an instability which causes audible low-frequency [[radio wave]]s to be emitted in the magnetosphere in the form of [[Whistler (radio)|whistler waves]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sudan|first=R. N.|date=1963|title=Plasma Electromagnetic Instabilities|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=6|issue=1|pages=57–61|doi=10.1063/1.1724508|bibcode=1963PhFl....6...57S|issn=0031-9171}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sudan|first=R. N.|date=1965|title=Whistler (or Helicon) Instability in Plasmas with Electron Beams|journal=Physical Review|volume=139|issue=1A|pages=A78–A82|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.139.A78|bibcode=1965PhRv..139...78S}}</ref> He also pioneered the study of the generation and propagation of intense [[ion beam]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Neri|first1=J. M.|last2=Hammer|first2=D. A.|last3=Ginet|first3=G.|last4=Sudan|first4=R. N.|date=1980|title=Intense lithium, boron, and carbon beams from a magnetically insulated diode|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=37|issue=1|pages=101–103|doi=10.1063/1.91677|bibcode=1980ApPhL..37..101N|issn=0003-6951}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sudan|first=R. N.|date=1976|title=Propagation and Defocusing of Intense Ion Beams in a Background Plasma|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=37|issue=24|pages=1613–1615|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.1613|bibcode=1976PhRvL..37.1613S}}</ref> and contributed to theories of [[plasma instabilities]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Denavit|first1=J.|last2=Sudan|first2=R. N.|date=1975|title=Whistler sideband instability|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=18|issue=5|pages=575–584|doi=10.1063/1.861173|bibcode=1975PhFl...18..575D|issn=0031-9171}}</ref> and plasma turbulence.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Similon|first1=P L|last2=Sudan|first2=R N|date=1990|title=Plasma Turbulence|journal=Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics|volume=22|issue=1|pages=317–347|doi=10.1146/annurev.fl.22.010190.001533|bibcode=1990AnRFM..22..317S}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Sudan studied at Punjab University (Bachelor's degree in 1948) and at the [[Indian Institute of Science|India Institute of Science]], where he received his diploma in 1952. In 1955, he received his doctorate in electrical engineering from [[Imperial College London]], where he was a Tata Fellow. He then worked as an engineer at the [[British Thomson-Houston Company]] until 1957 and then at [[Imperial Chemical Industries]].

From 1958, he was a scientist at [[Cornell University]] (in Simpson Linke's electrical engineering laboratory). His studies of power cut-off devices there led him to plasma physics. In 1959, he became assistant professor there and 1968 professor of electrical engineering and applied physics. He was IBM Professor of Engineering there from 1975 and from 1975 to 1985, the director of the Laboratory for Plasma Studies. He retired as Professor Emeritus in 2001.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=University|first1=Cornell|last2=Faculty|first2=Office of the Dean of the University|date=2009|title=Sudan, Ravindra Nath|url=https://ecommons.cornell.edu/handle/1813/19188|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 1984, he founded the [[Cornell Theory Center]] with [[Kenneth G. Wilson]] and was its deputy director from 1985 to 1987. In 1970–71, he headed the theoretical plasma physics department at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory|US Naval Research Laboratory]]. From 1970 to 1973, he was a visiting scientist at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|International Center for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in Trieste and in 1975 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton University|Princeton]]. In 1983, he was a Senior Research Fellow of the Fusion Research Institute at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].

== Honors and awards ==
In 1968, Sudan was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1968&unit_id=DPP&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|last=|first=|date=|website=www.aps.org|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref> In 1989, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Sudan&first_nm=Ravindra&year=1989|title=1989 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref> In 1994, he received the gold medal from the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" />
